decisions.title: acp.research.v1@1.0.0 is the single extension version authority; acp/mcp_extension.py is its only executable spelling
decisions.decision: The research extension identity is acp.research.v1@1.0.0 and has exactly one authority: p2-research-operations.v1.json::client_path.negotiation (extension_id + extension_version). application-api.v1.json::mcp_extensions['acp.research.v1'] is a projection that must equal it (version, negotiated_in, negotiation_tool, negotiation_request_field, initialize_claim, implemented, negotiated_default). The only executable spelling of the id/version pair on the acp side is src/acp/mcp_extension.py (RESEARCH_EXTENSION_ID / RESEARCH_EXTENSION_VERSION -> ExtensionSpec), injected by acp.services_mcp_bootstrap and acp.api.routes into acp_services.entrypoints.mcp.negotiate_research_extension(spec=...). acp_services defines no extension id/version constant: it receives the spec parametrically and assembles its own acp.negotiation.v1 id from chr(97) because the Services isolation gate forbids acp.* wire literals. RPH mirrors the pair in rph/packages/bridge/src/index.ts::BRIDGE_EXTENSION_ID/BRIDGE_EXTENSION_VERSION. A version bump edits the P2 authority, this projection, src/acp/mcp_extension.py and the bridge constant in one change, with a new negative sample.
decisions.rationale: M0-09 fixed the carrier but left the version question open for M1-01, and the pair already existed in four places with two historical values (the B06 drift wrote 1.1.0 where the extension is 1.0.0). Freezing one authority now prevents a partial bump from re-introducing a 'which version is real' choice inside M1-01.
decisions.rollback: No storage and no consumer schema changes: rollback is to revert the contract field, the constant in src/acp/mcp_extension.py and the bridge constant together, which restores the previous advertisement for every client in the same request. A partial revert is forbidden because it serves an id/version pair the other surfaces do not declare; a client that cached the old advertisement is answered by the same acp_capabilities refusal path (unsupported_capability), never by a silent downgrade.

decisions.title: The research extension negotiates in tools/call acp_capabilities; initialize never declares a negotiated state
decisions.decision: The extension handshake carrier is tools/call:acp_capabilities with request field research_extension{id,version}; the frozen values are request_carrier=tools/call, request_tool=acp_capabilities, request_field=research_extension and initialize_claim=none. initialize may only point at the carrier through capabilities.extensions['acp.negotiation.v1'].extension_handshake: it must not advertise acp.research.v1 and must not carry any 'negotiated' assertion, in the top-level result or inside capabilities. The only surface where advertised / implemented / negotiated appear is the acp_capabilities result extensions[], where negotiated_by is always tools/call:acp_capabilities, implemented is derived from the registered allowlist covering RESEARCH_TOOL_NAMES (the ten P2 tools), and negotiated=true requires implemented=true AND a requested version equal to the authority version. Refusals are typed in-band: unsupported_capability with params.rule in {extension_not_advertised, extension_version_mismatch, extension_not_implemented, extension_not_negotiated}, and a project-scope mismatch answers access_denied + params.rule=project_scope_mismatch while still returning extensions[]. Advertising is never delivery.
decisions.rationale: The frozen DSH client hard-codes capabilities:{} and drops a top-level initialize extensions block, so an initialize-based claim is unobservable (M0-08/M0-09). Without a frozen carrier and a frozen negotiated rule, M1-01 could move the claim back into initialize or promote advertising to delivery.
decisions.rollback: Wire-only: reverting means restoring the previous contract block and the previous server build in one deploy; there is no stored negotiation state to migrate. Clients that cached a tools/call advertisement re-read it on the next acp_capabilities call, and clients that never call it see no research surface at all (unknown_tool), which is the same failure mode as before the extension existed.

a second carrier or a second client protocol for the extension

decisions.title: Branch decision external_change_not_required: M0-13 is NOT_APPLICABLE with named reopen conditions
decisions.decision: M0-09 selected path_selected / application_level_handshake_tools_call, therefore no upstream DSH client capability option, official adapter change, fork, patch, lock bump or BOM entry is required: M0-13 is NOT_APPLICABLE with reason external_change_not_required and is not a predecessor of M1-01. The branch is reopened only by an explicit decision: (a) the upstream client (or an official adapter) begins offering a capability option that can carry acp.research.v1 in initialize — then a new ADR plus a scope_change decision reopens M0-13 and makes it a mandatory M1-01 predecessor; (b) the research product path is abandoned — then scope_change applies, M1-01 freezes only the eight P1 tools, the research extension stays DEFERRED, the M3 agent research line does not start, and complete ACP2 stays NOT_VERIFIED. Neither branch may be entered silently inside M1-01, and no private untransferable patch may be used to freeze M1.
decisions.rationale: The plan requires an explicit branch. Recording NOT_APPLICABLE without the conditions that would overturn it lets a later implementer change the carrier or abandon research without a scope decision, which is exactly the 'choose during implementation' failure M0-12 exists to prevent.

decisions.title: Contract mutation ownership: P2 authority -> application-api projection -> launch descriptor, one change set with ADR, sample and digest
decisions.decision: The negotiation surface has exactly three contract files in authority order: (1) p2-research-operations.v1.json::client_path.negotiation is the authority for id/version/carrier/request field/initialize_claim/refusal rules; (2) application-api.v1.json::mcp_extensions['acp.research.v1'] is a projection that must equal it; (3) mcp-launch.schema.json + mcp-launch.template.json carry descriptor metadata only, where initialize.extensions['acp.research.v1'].negotiated is const false and never a negotiated claim. Any mutation must, in one change: (a) amend ADR-006 with a new or amended D-decision first; (b) update all three files plus the code constants (D-INT-01) and the RPH mirror; (c) add or update a positive/negative sample under runtime/samples/application-api/; (d) recompute the file sha256, the manifest contract entry digest and contract_digest with validate_acp2_contracts.py; (e) leave the eight P1 tool names and input schemas unchanged. Forbidden: editing the projection without the authority, moving negotiation back into initialize, adding a second client protocol (restricted HTTP path), or publishing a descriptor with negotiated other than false.
decisions.rationale: M0-08/M0-09 had to repair a projection that drifted from its authority (1.1.0) and a launch descriptor that claimed negotiated=true. The plan makes contract mutation an explicit, reviewable path, so M1-01 must not be able to edit one surface and leave the others inconsistent.
decisions.rollback: Contract files are versioned bytes: rollback is a revert commit plus a digest recompute (file sha256, manifest entry, contract_digest) in the same change, and no runtime state depends on the edit. A revert must keep the three surfaces consistent; reverting only the authority leaves a projection that names a nonexistent carrier, which validate_acp2_contracts.py and the M0-12 validator both reject.

decisions.title: CI required scope: contract marker owned by mcp-conformance, DSH declared not vendored, frontend and RPH gates mandatory
decisions.decision: The required CI surface is: (1) the py3.10/3.11/3.12 matrix runs compileall plus pytest tests/ -m 'not slow and not contract' and never satisfies the contract gate; (2) exactly one lane owns the contract marker — mcp-conformance (Python 3.11 + Node 22.19.0 + pnpm 11.28.5) — and it runs a non-empty non-contract structural subset first, then test_acp2_mcp_sdk_contract.py -m contract with JUnit skip accounting where an empty selection, a partial skip or an available-but-skipped run all fail; (3) the frozen DSH tree is never vendored: it is declared only through the repository variable ACP2_DSH_SOURCE, an unset variable reports NOT_VERIFIED with exact counts, and a declared-but-unresolvable tree fails DSH_DECLARED_BUT_UNRESOLVED; (4) frontend-module-tests is a mandatory job with a non-empty *.test.js guard and run_all.js exit 1/2 semantics; (5) the rph job runs only when rph/pnpm-lock.yaml exists, runs install --frozen-lockfile, build, test, check, package, and uploads the offline install surface rph/dist-packages/* with if-no-files-found: error; (6) every job records wall-clock and a leg over 20 minutes must be split, never skipped; (7) the ruff lint/format steps stay commented until the independent hygiene stream lands (D-INT-06/D-INT-07) and are never cited as a gap gate.
decisions.rationale: M0-02a/b fixed four structural CI breakpoints (matrix/contract marker collision, frontend vacuum, RPH artifact before package, conformance placeholder) and M0-02b made the conformance lane a real gate. Freezing the scope prevents M1 from 'closing' G20 with a lane that skips, an empty selection or a vendored tool tree, and prevents the lint gate from being used as a substitute.
decisions.rollback: CI is executable YAML, so rollback is a revert commit of .github/workflows/ci.yml plus tests/test_ci_workflow_contract.py in the same change; the contract gate must never be rolled back to a report-only step or to the ordinary matrix, because that would re-open the G20 vacuous-pass path. A rollback that keeps the lane but drops the skip accounting is forbidden.

decisions.title: Ruff is an independent hygiene stream and is never a G01-G26 required closing condition
decisions.decision: Ruff 0.15.22 is the reviewed version, but the ratchet is a separate hygiene flow. The baseline is regenerated only in a dedicated lint-cleanup or Ruff-upgrade PR; feature and remediation PRs never reset it; the baseline may only shrink; format checks are scoped to the touched files and must be empty-selection safe. `ruff check` / `ruff format` never become a required gate for closing G01-G26 or any M0/M1 exit, and no gap may be closed or kept open on the basis of a ruff count. Historical counts (ci.yml's ~678 errors / 63 files, the independent review's 1,065 diagnostics / 130 files, 182 unformatted files) are trend-only and are not comparable to each other or usable as a baseline. The release scope records the same exclusion as SCOPE-OUT-07.
decisions.rationale: The plan deliberately split hygiene out so that a legacy lint backlog cannot be used either as a blocker or as evidence of progress. Without freezing the exclusion, M0-02c's pending ratchet could be cited as a closing condition for G20 or as a reason to hold M1.
decisions.rollback: Policy only, no wire or storage surface. Rollback would require a new plan amendment that makes lint a required gate; until then a feature PR may not re-enable the lint steps, regenerate the baseline or cite ruff counts as evidence. If lint is ever promoted, it needs its own decision and its own reproducible baseline receipt.

decisions.title: decision-freeze registration: both freezes are delivered contracts with file sha256, owner INT, stage M0-12
decisions.decision: Both freeze documents are delivered contracts of the ACP 2.0 contract set: decision-freeze/identity.v1.json (id decision-freeze-identity) and decision-freeze/integration.v1.json (id decision-freeze-integration). Each manifest entry is {id, path, status: delivered, owner: INT, delivered_by: M0-12, sha256: sha256 of the file bytes at registration time}. The digest is never embedded in the freeze itself (self-reference) and identity.v1.json's digest is always recomputed from the committed bytes, so the other lane's D-IDENT-10 flip cannot leave a stale digest behind. Registration also recomputes contract_digest and the manifest self digest and bumps the manifest contract_version. Two validator deltas are mandatory because scripts/acceptance/validate_acp2_contracts.py currently accepts owner in {A,B,C} and DELIVERED_IDS_BY_STAGE has no M0-12 stage: (1) add 'M0-12' -> {decision-freeze-identity, decision-freeze-integration} to DELIVERED_IDS_BY_STAGE; (2) accept INT in the contracts[].owner enum (the recorded choice; the alternative mapping to owner B with an INT signoff is rejected because it would hide the aggregating owner). M0-12 does not edit the manifest: the orchestrator executes the registration after the merge.
decisions.pending_reason: Manifest single-writer rule: this task records the registration decision and the entry shape only. docs/reference/next-change/acp2-contracts/manifest.json is not modified by M0-12, so neither freeze is registered yet; executing also needs the two validator deltas above plus a manifest contract_version bump and digest recompute.
decisions.rationale: The contract set is the H0 index for every downstream task, and the identity freeze deliberately left registration to M0-12. Recording the exact entry shape and the two validator deltas makes the registration a mechanical edit instead of a new decision, and keeps the digest rule out of the file itself.
decisions.rollback: Registration is additive metadata: rollback removes both contract entries and recomputes contract_digest plus the manifest self digest, and must revert the manifest contract_version bump with it. The freeze files themselves stay in git; unregistering them does not delete evidence.
